result.competitor: The MA and MN state portals are free to use; MN accepts an Excel ledger and MA accepts online entry only. PlotBox cemetery software tracks endowment and preneed trusts, produces a Fund Activity Report and exports in the trustee's format, but it does not claim to produce state forms. Bank trustees and master trustees supply year-end statements, and in some states, such as OR, the trustee files its own report. Funeral software such as The Professional Programs covers preneed. Osiris and FrontRunner came up in no search results, so their coverage was not checked. No product was found that fills in state report forms across many states.
result.duty: Annual preneed trust and perpetual-care fund reports filed by funeral homes and cemeteries with state boards. Examples: MT MCA 35-20-315, report due January 1 (ARM 24.147.1604 adds a fine of up to $1,000 and voids the licence if not filed). MN preneed trust report due March 31, filed electronically. MA 239 CMR 4.12(5), online-only, due January 31; the June 30 date in the claim comes from an outdated 2014 form. OH OAC 4717-10-01, due March 31. CA due May 1 with a CPA audit. VA due within 4 months of fiscal year end. MD due within 150 days, with a CPA audit. The rules are in force but every state is different, and insurance-funded preneed is often exempt.
result.market: NFDA counts about 15,401 US funeral homes, most of them family-owned; IBISWorld counts about 29,148 businesses. The number of cemeteries was not found (not_reached). The duty applies only to the share holding trust-funded preneed or perpetual-care funds, and that share varies by state.
result.reason: The duties are real and in force, but the rules differ by state. MT MCA 35-20-315 requires a January 1 report to the district court, and licensed MT cemeteries also file a Board report; missing it can bring a fine of up to $1,000 or void the licence. MN wants an electronic preneed trust report by March 31. MA now requires an online report by January 31, not June 30 as the claim says. OH files by March 31, and CA, AZ, MS, FL and VA have their own rules. Each filing happens once a year and some states require CPA audits. MA and MN run free state portals, and MN accepts an Excel ledger. PlotBox tracks trust funds and exports data. No vendor was confirmed to produce state forms. There are about 15,401 funeral homes.

result.competitor: I found no software that tracks contractor licence, bond or certificate renewals. Searches returned only DOL and state guidance and job postings. The DOL contractor lookup lists and the state portals (CA DLSE online renewal) are free. Surety bond vendors (suretyone, bryantsuretybonds, suretybonds.com) handle the bonds and probably send renewal reminders (not checked). Farm payroll tools named in the claim (FieldClock, Seso, TaxBandits) cover payroll and records but were not checked for licence tracking. One blog (beancount.io) has a WH-540 guide, but it is content, not a product.
result.duty: Federal MSPA: a contractor and each crew employee doing contracting work must hold a WHD certificate (WH-530/WH-540) before acting. Housing and transport need separate authorisation. DOL publishes lists of active certificates only. The DOL resources page lists PDF forms only and mentions no online filing portal. Renewal timing and penalty amounts were not checked this session. California: DLSE licence renewed at least 60 days before expiry (online via permits.dir.ca.gov/FLC_External or form DLSE 401-R), with a payroll-tiered bond (8 CCR 13664), DE 9 wage returns, a workers' comp certificate and 8 hours of education per licence period. Oregon: 12-month licence, renewal due 1 month before expiry, 2- or 4-year terms available later. Washington: L&I annual licence and bond. AB 1362 is chaptered (Ch. 190, Stats. 2025, signed Oct 1 2025): H-2A foreign labour recruiter registration and bond from July 1 2027. The bond figures ($50k-$150k+) come from secondary summaries and were not checked against the bill text.
result.market: California: 1,504 contractors in 2021 (an industry association figure; it was 1,193 in 2016). Washington: more than 250 licensed (undated article). L&I publishes a licence list updated June 2026, but I did not count it. The total number of federal MSPA certificate holders is not published as a figure; it would have to be counted from DOL's Tableau list. The number of H-2A contractors affected by AB 1362 was not found. My estimate is a few thousand contractors nationally, with the most in CA, WA, OR and FL.
result.reason: The duties are real. Contractors must hold a federal MSPA certificate (WH-530) before doing any farm labour contracting, and they are liable for their employees' certificates. California requires a licence renewed at least 60 days before expiry, a bond sized by payroll (backed by DE 9 wage returns), workers' comp proof and 8 hours of classes. Oregon's licence lasts 12 months. AB 1362 is chaptered (Ch. 190, 2025) and adds registration for H-2A recruiters from July 1 2027. I found no tracker that does this job. But the market is small (about 1,500 CA contractors in 2021, roughly 250+ in WA), renewals come once a year, surety brokers already send reminders, and the work is mostly calendar reminders. Willingness to pay is likely low.

result.competitor: Several products already do the core job. Invenco Insite360 Comply. EKOS Fuel Sites: digital inspections, automatic tank gauge integration and central records, free trial, aimed at multi-site operators. Canary Compliance: record-keeping for gas stations. Crompco: the Vault SaaS platform plus managed compliance, and its customers include independents. Tanknology: 24/7 customer portal for compliance records. Seneca Compliance Manager. FleetRabbit (municipal fleets). GoCanvas and Paperform offer ready-made monthly UST checklist apps; DocHub hosts a fillable form. Many states publish free walkthrough checklists (AR, HI, SC), and Utah has its own state inspection app. I found no cheap, state-form-aware app aimed specifically at single-site owners, but the core job is already covered.
result.duty: Federal rule 40 CFR 280.36, enforced through state UST programs, in force since October 13, 2018. Every 30 days owners must check spill-prevention equipment (or before each delivery if deliveries are less frequent) and release-detection equipment. Containment sumps and handheld detection equipment are checked once a year. Walkthrough records must be kept for 1 year; some states require more, e.g. Illinois wants 2 years kept on site. States such as AR, SC, MI, OR and HI publish their own forms and checklists. Penalties are imposed under each state's UST enforcement program; I did not look up specific penalty amounts.
result.market: EPA's FY2025 report gives about 190,000 regulated facilities, covering roughly 533,277 active USTs. The extracted PDF text was cut off at that point, so the tank count is my reconstruction and should be checked against the PDF. The same report puts walkthrough compliance at 83.3% and overall technical compliance at 62.9%. I did not find how many of these are single-site independents.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under 40 CFR 280.36, UST owners must do a walkthrough every 30 days and an annual check, and keep the records for at least one year; Illinois requires 2 years kept on site. But several products already do the core job. Digital walkthrough forms, records and ATG data are covered by Invenco Insite360 Comply, EKOS (which offers a free trial), Canary Compliance, Crompco's Vault, Tanknology's records portal and FleetRabbit, and GoCanvas and Paperform have ready-made templates. Many states give the checklist away free. EPA's FY2025 walkthrough compliance rate is already 83.3%, so the pain is modest. Many owners' automatic tank gauges already record release-detection data. Single-site independents would likely pay little, and fuel distributors or testing contractors often bundle this compliance work. A niche could still exist for a cheap app that knows each state's forms.

result.competitor: Treez has an "AZ MET Report dashboard" that its help page says lets you "easily and accurately fill out" the MET-1. It replicates the inventory schedule on page 2 and exports a CSV to paste in. It does not compute the tax or file. Treez also has state tax guides for California, Illinois and New York. BLAZE calculates excise tax for distributors. Cannabis CPA and bookkeeping firms (Citrin Cooperman, Canethics, Kind Accounting, Cannabis Accounting Group, Taxfyle) offer bookkeeping and tax services; Canethics explicitly lists payroll and sales taxes. Filing is done on free state portals: CDTFA online, AZTaxes, and email or a spreadsheet for the WA LCB. I found no Avalara cannabis excise product, and no MET-1 or LIQ1295 report from Dutchie, Flowhub or Cova (not found, not proven absent).
result.duty: The duty is real and in force. In Washington, WAC 314-55-089 requires a 37% excise tax and a monthly report and payment to the LCB by the 20th, on form LIQ1295 (Excel or PDF, emailed), even in months with no sales. WAC 314-55-092 adds a 2% per month late penalty, and missed reports can lead to license suspension or revocation. In Arizona, the monthly MET-1 includes an inventory schedule required by statute and must be completed before the TPT return. Treez says it is due by the 20th; I did not confirm that date on an official page. California requires a separate retailer excise return filed electronically through the CDTFA portal (quarterly in the example found), with a 10% late penalty and a 50% penalty for nonpayment. Nevada requires a monthly return by the last day of the following month, even with no liability. Maine requires Form CE. I did not check the effect of federal rescheduling.
result.market: I did not verify a current count. Pew (undated) says nearly 15,000 US dispensaries, including 3,659 in California. Twenty-four states plus DC have adult-use cannabis, and each has its own return format. Washington has roughly 400–500 retailers (not verified). Many licensees are multi-state operators rather than small firms.
result.reason: The monthly excise return duty is real, mandatory and enforced with license-level penalties. But the core data preparation already comes from POS and ERP systems: Treez ships an Arizona MET-1 report that maps directly onto the form. Once the POS totals exist, filing is a short form on a free state portal, and CPAs bundle it with the bookkeeping and 280E work cannabis firms already pay for. Every state has a different form, which breaks up the market for a solo founder. The industry also faces banking, payment and federal-status friction, and margins are squeezed. A small wedge remains: a cross-POS, multi-state return preparer for independents. Treez's existing Arizona report contradicts the claim that "no product prepares the return".

The duty is real. Maricopa requires a commissary visit log kept in the unit in permanent ink, plus a signed commissary agreement at permit renewal. Utah County requires a commissary log kept on the truck. Alameda asks for renewal applications two weeks before expiry, and Yuba requires an annual inspection. Rules and forms differ by county, and each vendor usually deals with one county. Competition is weak: GoCanvas log and agreement templates, a Paperform template, a tiny VendGuard listing (permit tracker, unverified) and custom-build pitches from RationalGo. No dominant dedicated product was found. Market is roughly 60-90k US food trucks (IBISWorld estimates conflict). Willingness to pay is low, the buyers are fragmented, and a county-by-county rules database makes the MVP heavy. Not searched: regional vendors, and the 'also_reported' cottage-food calendar idea.

The duty is real. Arizona requires the driller's report within 30 days (A.R.S. 45-600), Texas within 60 days, Montana within 60 days, and Mississippi within 30 days. Each state sets its own form and deadline. No multi-state filing router turned up. General well-drilling management software exists (a Guideflow roundup lists such tools, plus GoCanvas drilling templates and Well Logger), and none was confirmed to cover multi-state submission. State portals are free. Most drillers work in only one state, so a router has little value. I found no count of U.S. drilling firms, and the NGWA figure of 14,000 members includes scientists and international members. I did not fetch the CT, VT or MA pages, so their details are unchecked. A small niche, with no strong pain and weak willingness to pay. Score 2.

The duty is real but fragmented across states. NC requires hauler registration with a 5-year renewal. CA requires quarterly manifest submissions. MO requires monthly summaries plus tracking forms kept 3 years. TX requires a state-prescribed 5-part manifest and an annual report. Nevada requires semiannual reports. AR runs a free state e-manifest portal and app. I found no tire-specific hauler-side vendor; only generic GoCanvas manifest forms exist. Weak points: there is no national hauler count (CA has about 7,500 registered vehicles/year). States prescribe formats, and some have their own portals (AR, MI), so third-party submission is unlikely. Hauler registration is infrequent, so frequency is low. Haulers are small and have low willingness to pay. The market is niche, so I score it low. MI page fetch returned 403.

The duty is real. The revised CCR rule (40 CFR 141 Subpart O) applies from Jan 1 2027, with first reports due July 1 2027 per a vendor summary (120Water). The new summary section and language-assistance text apply to small systems. Annual CCRs already exist, so this is a recurring duty. The core job is covered, though. EPA's CCRiWriter is free and EPA says it will add new federal requirements. State generators and templates are free too (Arizona publishes a template). I did not find any 2027 CCRiWriter release, so the update is unconfirmed. About 28,800 very small community systems exist (FEMA figure, undated; roughly 59% of about 49,700). Willingness to pay is low and operators are hard to reach. The free-tool competition leaves little room for a paid kit.

The duty is real but fragmented. Hawaii requires monthly copies within 15 days (Cornell HI rule). Wisconsin requires an annual report, due Oct 30, filed by emailing an Excel file (DATCP page fetched). Minnesota requires daily sales records and 5-year retention. Utah takes submissions through a state portal (AIMS). Idaho requires aggregate county reports. I could not fetch the Massachusetts page (403), so I did not verify its online-only June 1 rule. Most states want a simple Excel export or printable records, so the pain is low and dealers can use existing ag-retail ERP and POS systems. I found no dealer-count statistics and did not check whether those systems export state formats. Each state is a small market, and states accept Excel or paper. The per-dealer value is low and each state needs separate work. Confirmed as a real duty, but a weak standalone product.

Duty is real: HB 1021 (eff. July 1 2024) requires Florida condo associations with 25+ units to keep a website or app, with records posted within 30 days. The compliance date was Jan 1 2026, so the deadline-driven rush has passed. Sources give no clear penalty. One summary says $500 minimum or $10-30 per unit, which I could not verify. I did not check the HOA 100-parcel rule, the SIRS deadline or market size against a register. Competition is crowded: SetMySite ($249/mo or $1,500 build), UpperBee, CondoControl, Concierge Plus, Paid Memberships Pro and management companies. The core job (a compliant site plus records posting) is already done by many vendors, so "nothing already does it" is only weakly met. Small self-managed associations are a fragmented, hard-to-reach buyer group.

Duty is real: 40 CFR 441 requires pre-June 14 2017 separators to be replaced by June 14 2027, with a one-time compliance report and ongoing inspection and maintenance records. Several vendor and association pages confirm the date and the 3-year records; I did not open the eCFR text, and I did not find a changed deadline. The core job is partly served by HealthFirst OnTraq, Solmetex, RationalGo and free MangoApps log templates. Local forms vary and I found no filing service. Pain is low because the filing is one-time and the records are only kept for inspection, and no POTW submission is routinely required. The replacement is a one-off hardware purchase, so the value sits with separator sellers. Market is roughly 100k offices (my recollection, not checked this session). Low willingness to pay for software alone; a 2027 deadline spike is possible.

Law is real (NY LLC Transparency Act, effective 1 Jan 2026), but by the later sources it applies only to foreign LLCs authorized in NY. Hochul vetoed the amendment that would have covered domestic LLCs, so domestic LLCs do not file (Eckert Seamans, Wolters Kluwer). Existing foreign LLCs file by 31 Dec 2026 (some sources say 1 Jan 2027); new ones within 30 days. The fee is $25, filed online at an open NYDOS portal. Penalties are AG fines up to $500/day and suspension. Annual statements are required. The buyer pool is small (foreign LLCs only), and the filing is a one-time, simple form already served by registered agents and filing services (Ocorian, Zenind). Not a good solo-founder recurring-compliance product. I did not check the NYDOS site itself, and found no count of foreign LLCs.
